name: allocVector
title: Allocates an empty vector, matrix or array

origin.description: Allocates a vector filled with one value, faster than the corresponding function in R.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: A numeric giving the number of elements. It is coerced with as.numeric and then truncated toward zero.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: A single integer, numeric, or logical value copied into every element. The result uses that storage mode. The default 0 is double.

origin.details: The installed function returns a vector of the same mode as value. A negative length, and a length that is NA, NaN, or infinite, is "Argument 'length' is negative". A length above 2^52 is "vector is too large".
origin.value: A vector of the requested length and the storage mode of value.

translation.description: Allocates a vector filled with one value.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Number of elements. Coerced like R as.numeric, then truncated toward zero. None is an empty length and is rejected. nan and infinities are reported as a negative length.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: One value copied into every element. A float is double, an int is integer, and a bool is logical. None is R's bare NA, which is logical. Integer NA is -2147483648. Double NA is nan. The default 0.0 is double.

translation.details: The fill lives in the Rust crate allocmatrix, ported from matrixStats src/allocMatrix2.c. The result is a 1-d array. A negative truncated length is "Argument 'length' is negative". That check happens before the value is inspected. A length above 2^52 is "vector is too large". A double zero, including -0.0, is stored as +0. Logical values are stored as int32: 1, 0, and -2147483648 for NA. Extra arguments are ignored.
translation.value: A 1-d NumPy array. float64 for a double value, int32 for an integer or logical value.
